rationale: Use own colour and zero-based coordinates modulo 3. Zeros at residues (0,1), (0,2), (1,1), and (2,1) become 4, 5, 6, and 3 respectively; other residues and nonzero colours stay unchanged. Demonstration 3 shows all four residue rules across its zeros.

Use own colour and coordinate parity. Zero becomes 3 at even-row odd-column positions, 4 at odd-row even-column positions, and 2 at odd-row odd-column positions. Colour 2 becomes 7 at even-row even-column positions. Demonstration 2 exhibits each change while retaining zeros at even-even positions.

Use own colour and border flag. Interior colours 1, 2, and 3 become 4, 5, and 9; border colour 3 becomes 0. Demonstration 1 retains border 1 and 2 while changing interior examples of all three colours.

Use own colour plus both row and column nonzero colour sets. In demonstration 2, the changed 3 has row set {2,3} and column set {1,3}; in demonstration 3, the changed 3 has those same sets. Demonstration 7 changes zeros with row set {1,2} and column set {2} to 5.

Use own colour and row nonzero colour set. Rows containing {1,2} change 1 to 8; rows containing {2,3} change 0 to 4; rows containing {1,2,3} change 0 to 7 and 2 to 6. Demonstration 2 shows all three row cases.

Use own colour plus row and column nonzero colour sets. In demonstration 5, the changed 2 has row set {1,2,3} and column set {1,2}, whereas both changed 3s have row set {1,2,3} and column set {1,2,3}. Demonstration 7 changes both 3s with row set {1,3} and column set {2,3} to 5.

Use own colour and border flag. Border zeros become 4 and border 3s become 9; interior zeros become 5 and interior 2s become 0. Demonstration 3 shows these changes while retaining interior 3s and border 2s.

Use own colour and row nonzero colour set. Zeros in rows with {1}, {3}, {1,3}, and {2,3} become 1, 3, 2, and 1 respectively. Demonstration 2 shows the latter three cases; demonstration 4 shows the singleton {1} case. Other row sets preserve zeros.
Use own colour and border flag. Border colours 0, 1, and 2 become 2, 0, and 4; interior zeros become 3. Demonstration 1 shows all these changes while retaining interior 1 and 2 and all 3s.

Use the complete 3x3 neighbourhood, including out-of-grid markers. Demonstrations 6 and 9 change the top-left zero to 2 where its in-grid neighbourhood is entirely zero. Demonstration 2 changes a bottom-edge zero with an entirely zero in-grid neighbourhood to 8; the distinct boundary patterns distinguish these outputs.
